study_identification.title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study applies neuroanatomical normative modeling to quantify and track individual-level brain structural changes over time in ADNI participants (cognitively unimpaired controls, MCI, and AD patients) using serial MRI data. The study aims to assess whether normative modeling-derived markers can (1) track disease trajectories, (2) predict progression from MCI to AD, and (3) relate to other common imaging and non-imaging AD markers including cognition, amyloid/tau PET, and genetics.

The remaining 30% of controls plus MCI/AD participants were used for application and comparison.

deviation_metric.answer: Regional z-scores (Z); outliers defined as Z < -1.96 (ventricular z-scores inverted to reflect expansion); total outlier count (tOC) = sum of outliers across 168 regions; rate-of-change in z-scores; rate-of-change outliers defined as more than 2 SD from mean rate-of-change in cognitively unimpaired ADNI controls (Z = -0.0009)
deviation_metric.reason: The deviation metrics are clearly and comprehensively defined, including regional z-scores, outlier thresholds, total outlier count, and rate-of-change outlier definitions.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: Extreme deviations from the norm, or 'outliers,' with lower cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were identified for each region, defined as Z < -1.96. Here ventricular z scores were inverted to reflect volumetric expansion. The number of outliers was summed across all 168 regions to give a total outlier count (tOC) for each participant. ... 'Rate of z score change outliers' was then defined if a rate of change was more than two standard deviations away from the mean in the ADNI controls (which was Z = -0.0009).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Multiple approaches were used: (1) Linear models tested rate-of-change in tOC between diagnostic groups adjusting for age, sex, and AC score (AD stage); quadratic time term added to model non-linear effects. (2) Linear mixed-effects growth models (lme4 R package) with random intercepts per subject modeled tOC as a function of time by diagnostic group. (3) Cox proportional hazards regression assessed whether 12-month tOC change predicted MCI-to-AD conversion within 36 months (median threshold = 3); baseline tOC also tested. (4) Linear regressions adjusting for age, sex, and education related tOC rate-of-change to cognitive composites (ADNI MEM, ADNI EF); interactions with diagnostic group tested. (5) Linear regressions adjusting for age and sex related tOC rate-of-change to amyloid PET SUVR and tau PET SUVR; interactions with diagnostic group tested. (6) ANOVA and linear regressions adjusting for age and sex tested associations between tOC rate-of-change and APOE ε4 status (homozygous, heterozygous, non-carrier) and polygenic risk score (PRS); interactions with diagnostic group tested.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Total outlier count (tOC) increased over time in AD and in MCI converters; tOC rate-of-change correlated with worse cognition, higher amyloid/tau burden, and APOE ε4 status, and predicted MCI-to-AD progression; hippocampus showed the highest rate-of-change outliers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across 1181 ADNI participants (Controls 291, MCI 682, AD 208; 3233 scans over up to 9.5 years, mean follow-up 2.4 years), regional z-score outliers (Z < -1.96) were summarized as total outlier count (tOC). AD patients showed increasing tOC over time (β = 0.38, p = 9.8×10^-13) with non-linear acceleration (time^2: β = -31.0, p = 0.0005; stronger in AD: β = -35.5, p = 0.06); mean rate-of-change in tOC was highest in AD (5.26 ± 9.85), intermediate in MCI (0.59 ± 4.57), and lowest in controls (-0.01 ± 1.90). MCI progressors had higher tOC increase (3.97 ± 11.27) than MCI stable (0.53 ± 4.61, p = 0.03); every 3-outlier increase in first-year tOC conferred 30.2% increased risk of MCI-to-AD progression within 24 months (HR = 1.09, 95% CI [1.06, 1.12], p = 1.4×10^-14). The hippocampus had the highest proportion of rate-of-change outliers (53% of AD patients); in AD, hippocampal outliers increased from 47% at baseline to 72% at 24 months. tOC rate-of-change associated with worse memory (β = -1.99, p = 2.0×10^-16), executive function (β = -1.77, p = 2.0×10^-16), higher amyloid PET SUVR (β = 0.006, p = 0.001), and tau PET SUVR (β = 0.03, p = 0.0001). APOE ε4 status related to faster tOC increase (ANOVA F(2,755) = 10.06, p = 4.8×10^-5), driven by ε4 homozygotes (β = 2.33, p = 0.003) and heterozygotes (β = 5.77, p = 0.018); no association with PRS (p = 0.23). AC score (AD stage) was significantly associated with tOC rate-of-change (β = 0.24, p = 7.5×10^-9).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Single-domain application (ADNI only) without external independent validation; no explicit normative model fit metrics (EV, MSLL) reported post-calibration; reference cohort demographics (age/sex) not detailed in this paper (referred to Rutherford et al., 2022); potential heterogeneity from mixed FreeSurfer versions (v5/v6) mitigated by calibration but not eliminated; threshold-based outlier definitions may affect sensitivity/specificity; reference dataset over-representative of European ancestry; ADNI participants predominantly European ancestry with early-to-intermediate AD stages and fewer comorbidities, limiting generalizability; within-subject noise remains in longitudinal data; cross-sectional processing pipeline (not longitudinal FreeSurfer) may increase variability; regions treated independently despite likely intercorrelation; test-retest reliability not assessed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Introduces longitudinal neuroanatomical normative modeling with transfer learning calibration to target domain; defines rate-of-change normative outliers based on control distribution; integrates multimodal markers (cognition, amyloid/tau PET, genetics, disease stage); uses AC score (amyloid-cognition) as continuous AD staging measure derived from latent time disease progression modeling; discusses potential clinical translation via Quantitative Neuroradiology Initiative (QNI) framework; suggests utility for clinical trial stratification and personalized outcome measures; proposes 12-month run-in period for risk stratification in trials; models and scripts openly available at BrainCharts GitHub repository (no raw data sharing needed for application).

general_notes.general_notes: Atlas: Destrieux (148 cortical regions) + aseg (20 subcortical regions) = 168 total regions. Ventricular z-scores inverted to reflect expansion as outliers. BrainCharts GitHub repository: https://github.com/predictive-clinical-neuroscience/braincharts. Statistical analyses in R v3.6.2; growth models using lme4 package; brain mapping using ggseg package. Total scans: Controls 661, MCI 1999, AD 573, Total 3233. Median scans per participant: Controls 3 (IQR 2), MCI 4 (IQR 3), AD 3 (IQR 2). Mean follow-up time: Controls 41.5 ± 28.2 months, MCI 32.2 ± 25.5 months, AD 23.8 ± 21.4 months. MRI scanners: 1.5T and 3T across 62 ADNI sites. Baseline AC score (predicted years since amyloid positivity): Controls -5.17 ± 5.83 (-15.3 to 9.8), MCI 7.0 ± 4.0 (-7.0 to 14.6), AD 12.9 ± 2.1 (2.5 to 16.5). APOE ε4 carrier status: Controls 32.6% non-carriers (n=194), MCI 55.6% non-carriers (n=332), AD 11.7% non-carriers (n=70). Some participants (18% controls, 12.7% MCI, 10.8% AD) showed negative tOC rates (fewer outliers over time), mostly <5 regions, potentially due to scan noise. In AD patients without left hippocampal rate-of-change outliers (47%), highest outliers were in left amygdala (29%), right amygdala (28%), and bilateral lateral ventricles (11%). Non-linear growth models revealed acceleration in AD (quadratic time term significant). MCI progressive vs stable: first-year tOC difference β = 4.47, p = 3.1×10^-15. Baseline tOC also predicted MCI-to-AD progression: every 3-outlier increase conferred 9.7% increased risk (HR = 1.03, p = 0.003). 'Control to MCI' and 'MCI to AD' converters (n=181) were removed from growth models to ensure diagnostic group stability. Transfer learning adaptation set: 70% CU controls randomly selected with stratification by site and sex.
